path: Brandão's bloc finalizes a two-name slate; Roseana negotiates MDB inclusion while Weverton leans on Lula alignment and mayors.
Campaign nationalizes around Lula; Roseana's name recognition holds in the interior, but machine support is split among three heavyweights.
Second votes scatter; Roseana finishes in the top two but a slate-backed rival edges her for first place.
Right fields several Senate names (PL, Novo, Viana); Marília Campos is consolidated as Lula's single name in Minas.
Pacheco hesitates; right fails to coordinate fully, while Campos gains recognition through Lula's campaign events.
Left vote concentrates on Campos, but a leading right name draws heavy double votes and finishes narrowly first.
PL prioritizes a younger bolsonarista name; Viana seeks a slate slot through his party and incumbency.
Campos consolidates left; right candidates compete for the second seat, with Viana squeezed by PL and Zema-backed names.
Right second votes flow to the PL-endorsed candidate; Viana finishes third or lower.
PL slates Azambuja plus an ally; Contar runs on his own bolsonarista base, while Trad leans on Riedel's coalition.
Left consolidates behind one name, taking a solid bloc; Contar, Trad and the left fight for second place.
Contar's 2022 base gives him strength but machine-backed Trad or the united left edge him out for second.
Azambuja secures the governing coalition and PL support; the left unites behind one candidate.
The right field splits between Azambuja, Trad and Contar, but Azambuja's machine and mayors carry the interior.
Azambuja tops the count; the consolidated left candidate is close but finishes behind him.
Mendes is the clear favourite; PL fields its own bolsonarista name, and Riva runs as MDB's bet.
The race for second becomes Riva against the PL candidate; Bolsonaro's brand nationalizes the contest in the agribusiness interior.
The PL candidate captures the polarized right second vote; Riva finishes third.
Mendes enters as favourite with state machine and agribusiness support; PL weighs its own candidate.
Bolsonaro camp mostly accommodates Mendes; no scandal emerges and his approval sustains a lead.
Mendes finishes first comfortably, with the PL name or Riva in second.
Helder launches with a dominant machine and COP30 visibility; Éder Mauro consolidates the bolsonarista vote.
Helder draws cross-ideological votes across Pará while the right splits between Éder Mauro and Zequinha.
Helder wins first place by a wide margin.
Lula bloc runs Humberto Costa and Marília Arraes together; Raquel Lyra's camp fields a right-of-centre name.
Marília's personal brand and Lula's strength lift her; Humberto relies on PT structure.
Marília and Humberto split left first votes closely; Marília edges ahead in one plausible path, but the margin is thin.
Fonteles finalizes a two-name slate; Castro gets a slot but a PT name gets equal billing. Ciro Nogueira runs.
The governor's popularity drives slate voting; second votes split between Castro and the PT partner.
The PT partner or Castro tops the count; Ciro trails. Castro finishes first in roughly a third of paths.
Deltan registers his candidacy; challenges are filed under Ficha Limpa while Filipe Barros gets Bolsonaro's endorsement.
Courts move slowly; Deltan campaigns but splits the anti-PT vote with Barros, while the left consolidates.
Deltan finishes in a close three-way race; the eligibility risk and the split make first place unlikely.
Fátima Bezerra heads the PT slate; PL fields its own pair, and Styvenson runs without a strong machine.
Styvenson's personal brand draws cross-ideological votes; Fátima's weak approval drags her.
Fátima or the PL lead name tops the count; Styvenson finishes in the top three.
Governor Rocha weighs a run; PL decides endorsements; Máximo pitches health credentials to the right.
Several right names compete for the same voters; PL's endorsement goes elsewhere or is split.
A PL-backed candidate or Rocha tops the count; Máximo is competitive but finishes second or third.
The left unites behind one PT name; the right splits among PL, PP and Novo.
Van Hattem campaigns nationally on anti-PT themes, but PL and PP candidates hold the bolsonarista base.
The single left candidate tops the count; Van Hattem contends for second.
Carlos Bolsonaro runs on PL; De Toni seeks an alternative path, possibly another party.
Bolsonaro family loyalty and carpetbagger criticism collide; Amin runs on the governor's slate.
De Toni's local base is strong, but voters split right second votes three ways; she wins first in a minority of paths.
PL endorses André David; the governor's coalition backs Vieira and Carvalho.
Machine-backed incumbents dominate; David has limited statewide recognition.
An incumbent finishes first; David finishes third or fourth.
Gomes secures the PL slot; post-Barbosa factions realign and Irajá seeks re-election.
The turbulent state machine splits; Gomes' congressional influence brings mayoral support.
Gomes is competitive for first but faces several viable rivals; first place is roughly a toss-up among three.
Helder leads; his coalition backs a second name, and Éder Mauro gets PL's slot.
Zequinha may run but the bolsonarista base largely sticks with Éder Mauro; Helder's second name gets machine backing.
Éder Mauro and Helder's ally contest second closely; Éder Mauro finishes second in about half of paths.
Lula bloc runs Humberto with Marília; Lyra's camp fields a strong right name.
Left first votes split between Humberto and Marília; the right concentrates on one candidate.
Humberto finishes in the top three; second place is contested with Marília and the right candidate.
Ciro runs for re-election; Fonteles fields a disciplined two-name slate.
Ciro's personal machine draws votes from mayors; slate discipline partially holds.
Ciro competes with the weaker slate name for second; he takes it in a substantial minority of paths.
Barros gets Bolsonaro's endorsement; Deltan's candidacy is challenged; the left consolidates.
Barros and Deltan split the anti-PT vote; the left candidate stays in the top two.
Barros finishes second only if Deltan falters or is excluded; otherwise third.
Castro runs for Senate on PL; Jordy competes for the second PL slot; left and Paes bloc field names.
PL right splits two ways; the left and the Paes candidate draw the urban vote.
Castro or the left name leads; Jordy contends for second but often finishes third.
Fátima heads the PT slate with Samanda as second name; PL fields a strong candidate; Styvenson runs.
Left voters split their second vote; Styvenson draws cross-ideological support.
Samanda finishes behind Fátima, Styvenson and the PL lead name; second only in a narrow path.
Rocha weighs a run; PL decides endorsements; Sílvia seeks a slate slot.
Right names compete for the same voters; Sílvia lacks PL support.
Sílvia finishes in the pack, second only if PL backs her or the field fragments.
Denarium runs and survives court challenges; Surita runs on her Boa Vista base.
Bolsonarista vote concentrates on Denarium; Surita competes with Mecias for second.
Surita's capital base carries her to second in a substantial minority of paths.
The left unites on one PT name; the right splits among PL, PP and Novo.
Van Hattem's national profile helps, but PL voters favour their own candidate.
Second place is a close fight between Van Hattem and the PL/PP name.
Tarcísio's coalition runs a coordinated pair; Marina is the Lula bloc's second name.
Left votes split between the PT name and Marina; the right pair stays disciplined.
The right takes the top two in most paths; Marina finishes second in a minority.
Guimarães seeks a coalition slot; incumbents Gomes and Irajá run.
Machine support fragments after Barbosa's removal; Guimarães builds regional support.
He competes for second with an incumbent; he finishes second in roughly a quarter of paths.
Flávio Bolsonaro and other right candidates split the anti-Lula vote; Lula relies on federal programs and Alcolumbre.
Evangelical vote leans to Flávio; Alcolumbre's machine is lukewarm but present.
First round is close; right fragmentation gives Lula a narrow edge in about half of paths.
PT state machine mobilizes for Lula; Flávio Bolsonaro campaigns to cut the margin.
Ciro Gomes' opposition stays local; no major scandal shifts the Northeast vote.
Lula wins Ceará's first round by a large margin.
